newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa maize estimate unchanged on harvest delay.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa maize estimate unchanged on harvest delay.

text.p: South Africa's National Crop Estimates Committee, said on Monday it had kept its 1997 maize and sunflower forecasts unchanged as there was no new information suggesting substantial changes from a month ago.

It said in a statement that in most maize-producing areas, too little maize had been harvested thus far to be able to deduce the extent of the discrepancy between the realised size of the crops and forecasts.

"The wet conditions which prevail in general delay the harvesting process and have an adverse effect on the quality of the maize..., while the sunflower seed crop could be severely damaged by wind," the committee said.
The 1997 commercial maize crop is expected to yield 7.660 million tonnes, but unseasonal rains in May and June have delayed the harvest which was supposed to have kicked off last month.
The 1997 crop is expected to comprise 4.139 million tonnes of white maize and 3.521 million tonnes of yellow, the committee said.
The estimate, which excludes around 550,000 tonnes of maize grown as subsistence food in South Africa's homeland areas, is sharply down on the 1996 commercial crop of 9.694 million tonnes.
The third official sunflower seed estimate for 1997 forecast a crop of 450,000 tonnes, also unchanged from last month. This is also well down on last year's 755,000 tonnes.
